title: EXP-029 — Button Component Recovery Across Verified Coupled Unload
objective: On one new User-scoped classic BuildFromScratch Form `FX_ComponentUnloadLab01`, create exactly one native Toolbox Button, assign only Name=`FX_ButtonUnload01`, record its exact visible property-grid Type label, perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save, close the target Form exactly once, verify the existing `Unload IDO Metadata With Forms` preference remains enabled without changing it, invoke `Form > Definition > Unload All Global Form Objects` exactly once, then reopen the target exactly once through the same Designer's Form-menu recent-forms entry. Verify the same scoped Form recovers `FX_ButtonUnload01` with the identical Type label. Treat the result only as UI-level recovery of this Button definition across the tested coupled-unload workflow; do not claim database durability, backend identity, Caption persistence, IDO-metadata semantics, or behavior of other component properties/types.

acceptance_checks.description: Before mutation, evidence records the fresh worker/session identity, proves a usable live workflow in User scope while preserving inherited state untouched, shows a settled rendered Select Form row whose Name corresponds to the exact known-existing positive-control Name filter with Case Sensitive unchecked, and proves zero case-insensitive Name matches for `FX_ComponentUnloadLab01`. A populated grid, stale row, or target-zero result does not substitute for the positive control. Inspecting visible Caption/Name columns is permitted without modifying those values. If the positive control cannot be established after the bounded fresh/corrected inspection, stop blocked without target creation or further retry. If a target match exists, stop blocked without altering it.

Evidence proves exactly one User-scoped classic BuildFromScratch Form `FX_ComponentUnloadLab01` was created through the fresh-dialog Classic/BuildFromScratch procedure with Save Template visibly unchecked, and the loaded Form identity is Name=`FX_ComponentUnloadLab01`, ScopeType=User, ScopeName=<current user>.
Before component placement, inspected evidence proves the target Form is clean and untouched and records the rendered canvas/component state without claiming complete component cardinality.

Exactly one native Toolbox Button creation operation is evidenced using the verified recipe, including its native Playwright mouse.click canvas-placement method when no semantic alternative is available and the current visible canvas is established; only Name is assigned to `FX_ButtonUnload01`. Authoritative property-grid/accessibility evidence records exact Name and the exact visible Type label before Save, with no unrelated component-property mutation. Failed targeting attempts must be recorded and must not result in a second component-producing click or expanded recovery.
Exactly one ordinary Designer Save is evidenced; afterward the target is clean and the component still reports exact Name=`FX_ButtonUnload01` and the identical Type label recorded in AC-4.

Exactly one ordinary target Form-tab close is evidenced; the target tab is gone, no unsaved-change or unexpected prompt appears, and the same Designer remains active. After close, the verified Web Client > Form > User Preferences > Behavior route visibly shows `Unload IDO Metadata With Forms` checked/enabled; it is left unchanged and preferences close without Save. The Designer View-menu preferences dialog and hidden/internal preference values do not satisfy this visible gate. If the checkbox is unchecked or cannot be visibly established, stop blocked before unload.

Exactly one `Form > Definition > Unload All Global Form Objects` invocation is evidenced after the target is closed. Post-action evidence shows no error/unexpected prompt, the target remains closed, the same Designer remains active, and no second unload or preference mutation occurred.

Exactly one reopen through the same Designer's Form-menu recent-forms entry is evidenced; the reopened Form has Name=`FX_ComponentUnloadLab01`, ScopeType=User, matching ScopeName, clean state, recovered component Name=`FX_ButtonUnload01`, and Type exactly equal to AC-4. If recent-forms is unavailable or session establishment is required after mutation, stop blocked.

Final read-only audit shows exactly one visible case-insensitive Select Form Name match for `FX_ComponentUnloadLab01`, re-confirms through Web Client > Form > User Preferences > Behavior that `Unload IDO Metadata With Forms` remains visibly checked/enabled and unchanged, reconciles exactly one Form creation, one Button creation, one Name assignment, one ordinary Save, one target close, one global-Form-object unload, and one recent-forms reopen, and proves experiment-authored repository changes are confined to the EXP-029 record and `evidence/EXP-029/`. The inventory result is limited to the inspected UI, not database uniqueness. The resulting finding is classified observed only; replay verification requires a later independent replay.

notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261007-182351-hVYe. EXP-028 completed blocked before target creation: exact target-zero evidence was obtained, but the required known-existing Select Form positive-control row did not settle to correspond to its displayed Name filter. This was a preflight blocker, not a Caption-editing failure, and changing the experiment topic does not resolve it. EXP-029 retains the same strict positive-control prerequisite and must stop before mutation if it cannot be established within the bounded inspection. The new capability is Button Name/Type recovery across the stronger coupled-unload boundary, extending the accepted, independently replay-verified EXP-027/R2 ordinary close/reopen workflow using the already replay-verified unload procedures in EXP-006-R2 and EXP-007-R2. EXP-027-R2 resolved native Playwright coordinate placement as recipe-authorized; it does not authorize arbitrary scripted mutations. EXP-007-R2 established the visible preference route as Web Client > Form > User Preferences > Behavior, rather than the Designer View-menu dialog. The existing enabled preference is read without change; this experiment tests the coupled sequence only and does not isolate or investigate its incidental IDO-metadata effects. Only one native Button creation and one Name assignment are permitted. A successful result is observed Button Name/Type UI recovery after one Save, close, unload, and same-Designer recent-forms reopen, not Caption persistence, database durability, or backend identity.
